title: Injectivity of the canonical affine tensor section map
statement: Let f:U → X be a morphism of schemes. Put A=f_*O_U, ρ:O_X → A its structure map, IA=f⁻¹A, r₀:f⁻¹O_X → O_U its adjoint structure map, and t₀=f⁻¹ρ. Let B be a commutative-ring sheaf on U, b:O_U → B and t:IA → B making a pushout of r₀ and t₀. For an open V of X put W=f⁻¹V, D=Γ(X,V), C=Γ(U,W), and δ=t_W ∘ η_{A,V}:C → B(W). Assume f is affine and V is affine. The constructed q of [stage3-affine-pushout-ring-section-map] is injective.

source.place: Tag 01SB affine reduction; Tags 01I9, 01IA and 01HV for affine pullback sections

proof.text: Apply quasi-coherent pushforward to the regular O_U-module: the regular A-module restricted to O_X is f_*O_U and is quasi-coherent.

Apply the sheaf-level regular-module comparison to identify tensorPullback(f_*O_U) with the regular B-module restricted along b, compatibly with the canonical pullback unit. This isolates the regular-module specialization of pushout cancellation.

Use the affine module section comparison for G=f_*O_U on V and W=f⁻¹V, with W affine. Rewrite appLE at the identity inclusion to f.app V. Compose tensor swap, the affine comparison, and the section isomorphism e. The unit formula and O_U-linearity agree with affinePushoutSectionMap_tmul on pure tensors. Tensor induction proves equality on every tensor; injectivity follows by cancellation of e, the affine comparison, and tensor swap.

proof_origin.place: Lean reduction through sheaf-level regular-module identification, quasi-coherent pushforward, affine-section specialization, tensor induction, and injectivity cancellation
